detail.fact: SaaS-OMS proven pattern - THREE INDEPENDENT ORDER STATUS AXES (ADR-06): payment_status (unpaid/partially_paid/paid/refunded), fulfilment_status (new/allocated/picked/packed/shipped/delivered), exception_status (none/on_hold/cancelled/returned). Each enum owns allowedNext(); a cross-axis OrderStateMachine owns rules no single enum can know. Solves COD packed-but-unpaid and shipped-then-refunded without hybrid states. Status columns excluded from fillable; only the state machine writes them via forceFill inside DB::transaction
detail.source: Explore agent read SaaS-OMS app/Domain/Orders/OrderStateMachine.php, enums, migrations

detail.fact: SaaS-OMS proven tenancy pattern: single DB, row-scoped, NO package. TenantContext::idOrFail() THROWS when unresolved because returning null compiles to 'tenant_id IS NULL' and silently returns every unassigned row - throwing turns a data leak into a loud failure. BelongsToTenant auto-stamps on create, refuses cross-tenant creates, makes tenant_id immutable. Single greppable escape hatch Model::acrossTenants(). NO Gate::before super-admin bypass. Composite (tenant_id,id) FKs on 10 edges so the DB itself rejects cross-tenant references
detail.source: Explore agent read SaaS-OMS TenantContext, BelongsToTenant, TenantScope, BasePolicy, migration 2026_07_27_100001

detail.fact: COMMISSION ANTI-PATTERN (found in all 3 prior projects): commission rate stored on a MUTABLE settings row with no effective dating. Editing commission_ranks.rate or commission_settings.rate retroactively changes what a re-run of a CLOSED period produces. Fix: effective-dated immutable rule versions (valid_from/valid_to, new row on edit) and stamp rule_version_id onto every commission row
detail.source: Explore agent comparative read of dzi-holistik, AgentStockit, SAAS-Agent-Management commission tables

detail.fact: COMMISSION ANTI-PATTERN: commission calculated INLINE inside a payment-gateway callback (AgentStockit PaymentController:36, SAAS-Agent PaymentController:208) with NO unique index and NO idempotency check. Gateways retry callbacks, so this creates duplicate money. AgentStockit PayoutService::createBatch() also sweeps approved commissions into payout_items but never flips them to paid - running it twice pays the same commission twice. Fix: queued job keyed on order + DB unique index on (order_id,user_id,type,level)
detail.source: Explore agent read of AgentStockit and SAAS-Agent CommissionService and PaymentController

detail.fact: COMMISSION ANTI-PATTERN: no reversal or clawback path exists in ANY of the 3 prior projects. Order refunded/returned/cancelled after payout leaves the commission untouched. dzi-holistik even HARD-DELETES a pending commission to correct it (CommissionService::discardStale). Money rows must never vanish. Fix: reversed state + contra entry referencing the original, event-driven on order cancel/return/refund
detail.source: Explore agent grep for void/reversed/clawback across all 3 projects - zero hits

detail.fact: BEST COMMISSION IDEA found (SAAS-Agent-Management-System): margin-as-commission. Direct commission = (buyer_price - upline_tier_price) * qty computed PER ORDER ITEM. The commission IS the price ladder, so no second rate to configure and no drift between pricing and commission. Also has the finest attribution grain of the three: order_item_id + source_user_id + approved_by on the commission row
detail.source: Explore agent read SAAS-Agent-Management-System/app/Services/CommissionService.php

detail.title: Client project, single company with multi-branch, no SaaS shell
detail.chosen: Build the company tenancy kernel (company_id + global scope) but NOT packages, subscriptions, platform-owner console or billing

detail.title: Stack: Laravel 12 + PostgreSQL 16 + Inertia/React 19/TS/Bootstrap 5
detail.chosen: Option 1, SMEOS lineage: Laravel 12 LTS, PHP 8.3, PostgreSQL 16, ULID keys, NUMERIC(15,4) with a bcmath Money value object, Inertia 3 + React 19 + TypeScript + Bootstrap 5, spatie/laravel-permission teams mode, Pest 3 + Larastan + Pint

detail.title: Authorization is Permission x DataScope, built into the kernel from commit one
detail.chosen: Scope stored on the role-permission pivot (role_permission_scopes) with values own/team/branch/company/all, resolved by a ScopeResolver and applied in the query layer through a Scopeable contract. Fail closed. Exactly one greppable escape hatch

detail.title: Attribution is its own polymorphic domain; first-touch wins on tie-break
detail.chosen: attributions + attribution_touches tables, polymorphic over Lead/Customer/Order. Every touch recorded. Commission credit goes to the FIRST touch (the marketer who originally generated the lead). Attribution resolved from the lead trail then FROZEN onto the order at creation

detail.title: Commission pays a percentage of FULL gross margin (sales - cost - shipping - fees - ad spend)
detail.chosen: Default commission plan strategy is PercentageOfMargin where margin = sales minus product cost minus shipping/postage minus payment fees minus allocated ad spend. Commission accrues PROVISIONALLY on estimates and is RESTATED at period close against reconciled actuals, with the restatement emitted as an audited adjustment entry, never a silent re-run

detail.title: Commission rules immutable and effective-dated; every commission stamps its rule version and basis
detail.chosen: commission_rules + commission_rule_versions with valid_from/valid_to, immutable after creation. Every commission row persists rule_version_id, basis_amount, rate_type, rate_applied and calc_inputs jsonb, plus a commission_sources join to every contributing order line. Calculation runs in a queued job keyed on the order behind a DB unique index. Reversal is a contra entry, never a delete. Payout posts to Finance in the same transaction

detail.fact: REPRODUCED 2026-08-15 in Brand New ERP P0: Pest's expect($x)->not->toContain('a', 'my failure message') PASSES UNCONDITIONALLY because the second argument is parsed as another EXPECTED VALUE, not a message. A company_id mass-assignment guard written this way sat green while the violation was present. Only a deliberately planted violation exposed it. Fix: expect(in_array($needle, $haystack, true))->toBeFalse('message'). General rule: toContain/toContainEqual take variadic expected values - never pass a message to them. Every negated guard assertion must be proven by mutation before it is trusted
detail.source: Planted company_id into Branch fillable; suite reported 49 passed. After rewrite it reported 1 failed, 48 passed

detail.fact: SELF-INFLICTED 2026-08-15 Brand New ERP P0: a line-based Python comment-stripper silently corrupted 12 PHP files. Cause: a single-line docblock '/** @return array */' matched the block-OPEN branch, set drop_block=True and continued WITHOUT testing the same line for the closing '*/', so every following code line was swallowed until the next '*/'. Files were left syntactically invalid; the failure surfaced only as a confusing Pest DatasetMissing error, not as a parse error at the edit site. RULE: any script that rewrites source must run a syntax check (php -l / node --check / python -m py_compile) over EVERY touched file in the same step, and must handle open-and-close-on-one-line before the open-only branch. This is the same class as the PowerShell BOM anti-pattern - a mechanical rewrite that reports success while producing unparseable files
detail.source: 12 files broken and restored by hand; verified with a full php -l sweep, 0 broken after repair

Pest installs phpunit as a transitive dependency and Pest's shim exits 1 with 'Please run ./vendor/bin/pest instead', so verify reports a FALSE FAIL on every Pest project regardless of suite health. detail.fact: LARAVEL 11/12 TRAP found 2026-08-15: $middleware->priority([...]) in bootstrap/app.php REPLACES the entire framework default priority list, it does not merge. Passing two classes left a 2-entry list with Authenticate absent, so a route middleware hoisted to position 0 ran BEFORE authentication and its abort(401) pre-empted the guest redirect. Symptom was a guest getting 401 instead of a redirect to /login, which reads like an auth-config problem, not a priority problem. Correct API: prependToPriorityList($before, $insert) / appendToPriorityList($after, $insert), which preserve the 13 defaults. Also note Illuminate\\Auth\\Middleware\\Authenticate is NOT in the default priority list, so it must be inserted explicitly if ordering against it matters. Guard with a test asserting index(Authenticate) < index(YourMiddleware) < index(SubstituteBindings)
detail.source: Reproduced and fixed in Brand New ERP P1; verified priority list went from 2 entries to 13 with correct ordering

detail.fact: PROCESS RULE reinforced 2026-08-15: a scripted string replace that does not ASSERT it matched is a silent no-op. Twice in this project a python replace ran, printed a success message, and changed nothing because a formatter (Pint) had already rewritten the anchor text - once leaving a broken middleware priority in place while I believed it fixed. Rule: every scripted edit asserts count==1 before writing, or uses an edit tool that errors on no-match. A rewrite that cannot fail is a rewrite that cannot be trusted
detail.source: Two occurrences in Brand New ERP P1; the third attempt used an assert and correctly caught the mismatch

detail.fact: ELOQUENT TRAP found 2026-08-15: a database column DEFAULT does not populate an in-memory model. Customer::create(['code'=>..,'name'=>..]) left $customer->currency NULL even though the column defaults to 'MYR', because the default is applied by Postgres on INSERT and never read back unless the model is refreshed. A price resolver then received null where a currency string was required and threw a TypeError. FIX: mirror every meaningful DB default in the model's protected $attributes array so the in-memory object and the persisted row agree before any refresh
detail.source: Reproduced in Brand New ERP P2 PriceResolverTest; fixed by adding $attributes defaults to 14 models

detail.fact: VERIFIED 2026-08-15: Laravel's decimal:N cast returns a STRING at runtime (number_format output), not a float - confirmed by get_debug_type on ProductVariant::selling_price and TaxRate::rate_percent. Larastan's stubs type it as float, which produces false 'expects string, float given' errors at level 6. Money safety is intact; the fix is explicit (string) casts at the boundary plus a unit test asserting the cast returns a string, so a future framework change to float is caught rather than silently drifting money
detail.source: php -r get_debug_type probe against both models

detail.fact: NAMING TRAP found 2026-08-15: Laravel pluralised model UnitOfMeasure to table 'unit_of_measures' while the migration created 'units_of_measure' (correct English). Nothing failed until first use. GUARD ADDED: a reflection-driven test asserting every Eloquent model maps to a table that actually exists (Schema::hasTable on getTable()). This catches the whole class of model/migration name drift at suite time rather than in production
detail.source: Caught by the isolation suite in Brand New ERP P2; guard now permanent in tests/Isolation/SchemaGuardsTest.php

detail.fact: P3 ORDER DESIGN (Brand New ERP): three independent status axes ported from SaaS-OMS ADR-06 and extended. payment_status unpaid/partially_paid/paid/refunded; fulfilment_status draft/pending/approved/allocated/picked/packed/shipped/delivered/completed; exception_status none/on_hold/cancelled/returned. Each enum owns allowedNext(); OrderStateMachine owns the cross-axis rules. FIXED the known OMS defect P1-25: the machine refuses PaymentStatus::Paid while paid_amount < total, so status can never contradict the money. Status columns and money totals are both excluded from Order fillable; the state machine is the sole status writer and OrderService the sole money writer, both enforced by architecture tests proven with planted violations
detail.source: Implemented and tested in Brand New ERP P3; 499 tests green

detail.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - reasonAgainst() returning a human sentence instead of a boolean. OrderStateMachine::reasonAgainst(Order, BackedEnum): ?string returns null when legal and a merchant-readable sentence when not, e.g. 'This order has already shipped. Record a return instead of cancelling it.' canTransition() is then just reasonAgainst() === null, and availableTransitions() filters on it, so the UI, the API error and the guard all share one source of truth. The same idiom drives OrderMutabilityPolicy::reasonLocked() and is the intended shape for the commission engine's explanation in P6
detail.source: Ported from SaaS-OMS and implemented in Brand New ERP P3

detail.fact: LARAVEL 11/12 TRAP found 2026-08-15: framework AUTO-DISCOVERS listeners in app/Listeners (any class with a handle() method type-hinting an event). Adding an explicit Event::listen for the same event/listener pair registers it TWICE, so every side effect runs twice. In Brand New ERP P4 this silently reserved stock twice per order line - a duplicate-inventory bug that looked like a reservation logic error, not a wiring error. Fix: rely on auto-discovery OR disable it, never both. GUARD: assert Event::getListeners(YourEvent::class) has exactly the expected count; the guard was proven by planting the duplicate registration and confirming both the guard and the behavioural test fail
detail.source: Reproduced in Brand New ERP P4: 2 reservations for 1 order line; fixed and guarded

detail.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - reservation-based inventory with a provable invariant. stock.on_hand is signed (a real warehouse goes negative after a miscount; refusing to represent it turns a counting error into a 500). available = on_hand - reserved is DERIVED, never stored. Reserving changes only reserved; only commit changes on_hand and writes an append-only movement. Every on_hand change writes a movement carrying quantity_delta and a denormalised balance_after, so SUM(quantity_delta) == on_hand is a testable invariant per stock line. All mutations take a blocking SELECT FOR UPDATE on the stock row (not SKIP LOCKED - last-unit scarcity is queue-and-wait), and commit/release take their own lock so a reservation cannot be discharged twice
detail.source: Implemented in Brand New ERP P4; oversell reproduces on 3 of 3 runs when the lock is removed

detail.fact: POSTGRESQL CONSTRAINT found 2026-08-15: 'FOR UPDATE is not allowed with aggregate functions'. A sequence allocator written as Model::query()->where(...)->lockForUpdate()->max('sequence') is invalid SQL on Postgres and fails at runtime, not at analysis. Fix: lock the LAST ROW instead of the aggregate - orderByDesc('sequence')->lockForUpdate()->first() - then compute next in PHP, plus a retry on unique violation 23505 to cover the first-insert race where no row exists to lock
detail.source: Reproduced in Brand New ERP P5 attribution touch sequencing; fixed and 18 tests green

detail.fact: TESTING NUANCE recorded 2026-08-15: layered defence makes single-mutation proofs inconclusive. The attribution reports carried company scoping on BOTH the attributions table and the joined orders table, so removing either one alone did NOT leak and the isolation test still passed - which reads like a weak test but is actually redundant protection. Only stripping EVERY filter from the query made the test fail (2 rows instead of 1). RULE: when a planted violation does not fail a test, determine whether the test is weak or the code is redundantly protected before concluding either; strip the whole layer to find out
detail.source: Three successive planted violations against AttributionReport in Brand New ERP P5

detail.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - attribution as its own polymorphic domain. attribution_touches is an append-only trail keyed (subject_type, subject_id, sequence); attributions holds ONE resolved row per subject and is polymorphic across Lead, Customer and Order. First touch wins for credit, but every touch is retained so last-touch and multi-touch reporting stay available and changing the credit rule is a rule change not a migration. An Order INHERITS from its lead (or the customer's own attribution) and is then FROZEN - re-attributing throws, because commission is paid on it. A converted customer inherits its lead's first touch. Unattributed is a valid first-class state, never defaulted
detail.source: Implemented in Brand New ERP P5; all 12 attribution questions answered by named tested queries

detail.fact: POSTGRESQL NULL-DISTINCTNESS TRAP found 2026-08-15: a UNIQUE index does NOT prevent duplicates when a participating column is NULL, because Postgres treats NULLs as distinct. A commission idempotency constraint on (company_id, order_id, order_item_id, recipient_user_id, plan_id, type) silently allowed unlimited duplicates for ORDER-LEVEL accruals where order_item_id is NULL - the exact rows the constraint existed to protect. Detected only because a test tried to insert a deliberate duplicate and no exception was thrown. FIX on PG15+: UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (...). Verified: after the fix, removing the application-level idempotency check produces a UniqueConstraintViolationException instead of a duplicate row
detail.source: Reproduced and fixed in Brand New ERP P6; proven by planted violation

detail.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - a commission that explains itself from data. Every accrual persists rule_version_id, basis_amount, rate_type, rate_applied and a calc_inputs JSONB holding the full margin decomposition (sales, cost, shipping, fees, allocated ad spend, each with a label and a human basis string). explain() then RENDERS that line rather than storing prose: 'Commission MYR 38.50 - Recipient: Ali (marketer) - Rule: "Facebook Campaign Margin" v1 (effective 2025-08-15) - 12% of MYR 320.80 - Sales MYR 1,000.00 - Cost MYR 520.00 - Shipping MYR 49.20 - Fees MYR 30.00 - Ads MYR 80.00 = MYR 320.80 - Order SO-00001 - Provisional'. Rule versions are immutable (DB trigger) and effective-dated, so a closed period can never be rewritten, and commissions are never deleted - a reversal is a contra entry with negated amount AND negated sources so the trail nets to zero
detail.source: Implemented in Brand New ERP P6; 23 tests covering all ten prior-art anti-patterns

detail.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - a minimal but real double-entry ledger for an SME ERP. accounts (asset/liability/equity/income/expense) + journal_entries + journal_lines. Balance is enforced three ways: the Ledger service refuses an unbalanced post with a readable message, a CHECK constraint requires total_debit = total_credit on the entry, and a per-line CHECK requires exactly one of debit or credit to be positive. journal_lines are append-only at the DB (UPDATE and DELETE both rejected) so corrections must be reversing entries. balanceOf() signs by account type and trialBalance() must always be zero - that single assertion catches almost every posting mistake. Commission flows through it properly: payable posts Dr Commission Expense / Cr Commission Payable, and the payout posts Dr Commission Payable / Cr Bank, so the payable account clears to zero
detail.source: Implemented in Brand New ERP P7; 19 tests including trial-balance assertions after issue, payment, void and payout
